description: Change of use from office (Class E) to a 13-room apart-hotel (Class C1) including conversion of G/F part-undercroft car parking spaces into habitable space, second floor extension, and associated external alterations
decision_conditions: The proposed development, by reason of the inadequate and inconsistent heritage information and drawings submitted in respect of the Grade II listed building (part of which falls within the application site) and its setting, fails to demonstrate that the proposal would conserve the significance of the listed building. The proposal is contrary to London Plan Policy HC1, Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 Policies HE1 and BE1, and Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 Policies DMHB1, DMHB2 and DMHB4.

The proposed development, by reason of the absence of essential hotel ancillary and back-of-house facilities and the lack of information on how the accommodation would be managed and operated, fails to demonstrate that it would function as a genuine aparthotel/visitor accommodation use. As submitted, the Local Planning Authority cannot be satisfied that the proposal achieves the required high standard of building and site design and would operate satisfactorily without harmful operational effects. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy DME5 and Policy DMHB11 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and London Plan Policy D3.

The proposed development, by reason of the failure to demonstrate a safe, suitable and deliverable means of access and servicing for the proposed use, including deliveries/servicing, refuse collection and guest pick-up/drop-off arrangements, has not been shown to be capable of operating satisfactorily in practice. The development appears to rely on access over third-party private land where the landowner has objected and disputes any right of access, such that the Local Planning Authority cannot be satisfied the scheme is self-contained or deliverable. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies DMT1, DMT2, DMT5 and DMT6 (and Appendix C) of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020), Policy DMTC1, and Policy DME5.

The proposed development would result in the loss of office floorspace within a preferred office growth location (Hotel and Office Growth Location: Uxbridge Town Centre). The proposal is not supported by the evidence required by Policy DME3 to justify such loss. In the absence of this information, the proposal represents an unjustified loss of office floorspace and is contrary to Policy DME3 of the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 (2020) and the National Planning Policy Framework objective of supporting economic growth.

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

On this decision notice policies from the Councils Local Plan: Part 1 - Strategic Policies appear first, then relevant Local Plan Part 2 (2020), then London Plan Policies (2016). Hillingdon's Full Council adopted the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 - Strategic Policies on 8 November 2012 and the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 2 on 16 January 2020.

In dealing with the application the Council has implemented the requirement in the National Planning Policy Framework to work with the applicant in a positive and proactive way. We have made available detailed advice in the form of our statutory policies from the  Local Plan Part 1, Local Plan Part 2, Supplementary Planning Documents, Planning Briefs and other informal written guidance, as well as offering a full pre-application advice service.

We have however been unable to seek solutions to problems arising from the application as the principal of the proposal is clearly contrary to our statutory policies and negotiation could not overcome the reasons for refusal.
